headline: Approved a letter of support for the Whitneyville Cultural Commons collaboration, due December 1, and an unattended child policy.
summary: Robert Sheimen of the Whitneyville Cultural Commons discussed a possible renovation of between $3 - $20 million. Melissa said the library is looking at moving the Whitneyville branch there, since the current site is not ADA compliant, and that a MUNIS report may be $70,000 below target.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the 10.13.26 meeting as amended, unanimously.
Approved the Unattended Child Care Policy as written, with all in favor.
Approved the 2027 calendar as written, with all in favor.
Approved writing a letter of support for the Whitneyville Cultural Commons collaboration by December 1, with all Board members in favor.

decision_titles: Letter of support for Whitneyville Cultural Commons collaboration
plain_text:
TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Library Board Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
6:00 PM, November 10, 2026 
 
 
 
Hamden Government 
Center 
Third Floor Conference 
Room 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel:  (203) 287-7070 
Fax:  (203) 287-7075 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL TO ORDER 
  
 Pat Sirulnick called the meeting to order at 6:01. 
2. ATTENDANCE 
  
 In person: Pat Sirulnick, Melissa Canham-Clyne, Marcia Romanansky, Anita Buckmaster, 
Phil Kuchuk 
Online: Brett, Zac Zuber-Zander, Alyssa Dansinghani, Mary Jean Brown 
3. PUBLIC COMMENT 
  
 No public comment. 
4. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES 
  
 
 
  a. 10.13.26  
  Jan Glover motioned to approve the minutes as amended. 
Phil Kuchuk seconded the motion. 
Motion unanimously approved. 
5. CORRESPONDENCE 
There will be a brief summary of the correspondence submitted between the last 
correspondence update and this one. This includes but is not limited to any 
correspondence with council members that members wish to submit for the record. It can 
also include written communication to the council from the administration, community 
members, etc.   
 No correspondence. 
6. REPORTS 
  
 Melissa reviewed: 
• Staffing scheduling 
• Christmas and New Years fall on Friday
o Floating Holiday Stipulation  
▪ Carried over into the New Year 
▪ Whole year to use 
o Anticipate early holiday closing 
• October Programming 
• Podcast 
o Approximately 6300 downloads 
Alyssa reviewed: 
• Staff Development Day 
  
7. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 
 
8. ANNOUNCEMENTS 
  
 
 
 a. FOHL Liaison 
       
  No updates. 
 b. Personal Board-related Goals 
 
 
 
 
       
  Pat discussed her progress with her personal goal of reaching out to a member of the 
Legislative council. 
 
No other members shared a goal. 
 c. Stakeholder Meetings 
       
  Board Members received a call to action by the Chair and the Executive Director to 
attend a stakeholder meeting, introduce themselves as a board member and thank 
people for attending. 
 
 
 
9. OLD BUSINESS 
  
 
 
  a. Unattended child policy
The Board discussed the prepared Unattended Child Care Policy. 
 
Jean motion to accept the document as is. Phil seconded. All were in favor 
  b. Financial update     
  Melissa discussed the following: 
• Gift Fund 
o Gift sent to Micheal after his sudden passing on behalf of the board 
• Restricted Friends money 
o Canva and SurveyMonkey subscriptions 
• Reimbursent 
• MUNIS REPORT 
o May be $70,000 below target 
o $70k cushion, spend the budget to $0 
• Uniform updates 
 
  c. Committee Reports  
 
  
  
 
 1. Finance 
 
 
       
   
Phil discussed the Hamden Public Library Fund and his meeting with Melissa. 
 
 
 2. Strategic Focus  
       
  Melissa updated the Board on: 
• Politician's community needs assessment conversation 
o In conflict with Lion meeting to advocate for more funding from CT 
State Library 
 
10. NEW BUSINESS 
  
 
 
  a. 2027 Calendar
Jan made a motion to accept the calendar as is. Phil seconded. All were in favor. 
  b. Collaborative Opportunity from Whitneyville Cultural Commons  
  Guest speaker, founding Executive Director and now Strategic Director of the 
Whitneyville Cultural Commons, Robert Sheimen discussed the following:  
• What are the needs of Hamden?  
• Renderings and sketches of possible scope 
• Between $3 - $20 million renovation 
• Treating Whitneyville as a walkable neighborhood 
 
Melissa discussed: 
• Looking at moving Whitneville branch over to the Cultural Commons for the 
following reasons: 
o Smallest and most used library 
o Not ADA compliant 
o Improvements on current location might be too costly for the town 
o Joint 3rd space, great for programming despite library staff shortages 
• Applying for a $2 million construction grant for Miller 
• Keeping the feel of the public library alive 
 
Jan motioned for the Board to write a letter of Support for the Cultural 
Commons collaboration by December 1st. Phil seconded. All Board members 
were in favor. 
11. ADJOURNMENT 
  
 Phil maded a motion to adjourn at 7:18PM.  
Jan seconded the motion. 
Meeting adjourned at 7:18PM.
